# 05 · Recurring Threads (SEALED — DM ONLY)

> The threads that run under the chapters: the rival, the neighborhood, gifts, the villains' footprints, discovery moments and Moss's return. Use this file between chapters to decide what the world is doing off-screen.

## 2. The rival: Rook (Danny Pratt)

**Who he is:** Ash's mirror. Same streets, same age, same quick hands, but he steals from anyone, including the Fringe, which Ash never does. Their rivalry goes back to age eight (a fight over a stolen pie; both claim they won). Rook's mother, **Martha Pratt**, is sick with lung-rot. Every coin he steals goes to her doctor and his own boots, in that order. He'd never say so.

| Ch | Rook does | Ash's opening |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hunts Thistle for the Bucket. Boasts at the well. | Beat him to the prize. |
| 2 | His Magpies try to lift Ash's courier parcel. | A rooftop chase; mutual grudging respect possible. |
| 4 | Enters the Bargerace against Ash and sabotages the poles. If the flood hits, he's seen carrying his mum out. | Ash can help him in the flood (+1 to his redemption). |
| 5 | **Bought by the Calm** (SEC-14). New boots, his mum's doctor paid. | Ash notices. Confronting him: "Everyone's bought, Fenwick. You just haven't had the right offer." |
| 7 | Leads the Calm crew over the Lane's roofs. | **Key choice.** If Ash helped him in the flood, or ever helped Martha, Rook hesitates and shouts a warning. If not, he follows through, and is captured or flees. |
| 9–11 | Redemption path: Rook brings information, steals the Mabry letters. Fall path: Rook goes deeper with the Calm and is half-Hushed by Ch11 (eyes faintly grey). | Ash can wake him (Ch15+) if fallen. |
| 12 | Redemption path: he steals the fire-night ledger for Ash (Route C). | |
| 13 | Redemption path: he runs the Market Steps district in the skill challenge. Fall path: he's one of the Hushed lamp-wardens in the Reserve, and can be woken mid-fight. | |
| 20 | He shows up at the gathering, either way. If redeemed: "Don't make it weird, Fenwick." | |

**Martha Pratt:** a free Mercy and rival lever. If Ash gets Moss (or Mother Brine) to treat her lung-rot, Rook's redemption is all but certain.

## 3. Willow Lane arcs (the people Ash is protecting)

| Person | Arc |
|---|---|
| **Bess Carter, Pip, Nell** | Ch1: doorstep gifts. Ch4: saved in the flood. Ch7: hide Lark (Pip and Lark become best friends; Pip's the first human Lark trusts). Ch11: Bess figures out who's been leaving the gifts and says nothing, but leaves a pie on the Fenwick step "for whoever." Ch13: Bess runs the Lane during Lantern Night. Ch20: Pip, 10, sneaks onto Driftmarket's barge to come to the gathering. |
| **Walt and Dora Finch** | Ch1: leaking roof. Ch4: Walt is Hushed in the flood (default). **Ch7–15: "Wake Walt" is a running thread.** Ash can't wake him until Ch15's discovery (or Clara and Ash's duet at Ch12). When Walt wakes, his first words are to Dora. Dora delivered the twins and knows about Wren (SEC-16). She's the one who slips. |
| **Netta Lowe** | Gossip engine, rumor source every session, and later the Lane's lookout. Ch13: she rings the well-bell to warn the Lane. |
| **Simon Shaw** | Ash's credit line. In Ch9 he's squeezed by a Merrow-owned debt, which gives Ash a personal reason to hit the House of Merrow. |
| **Peg Mallory** | The Willow is the Lane's living room. Ch4: the Willow can burn. Ch7: hides Lark in the cellar. Ch17: hosts the Fringe's march to the Concord. If the Willow burned in Ch4, the Lane rebuilds it in Ch7–11 (a side activity: Ash can steal the timber). |
| **Aggie Thorne** | Ch5: hurt defending Thistle. Ch7: tells Ash about Moss (SEC-20). Ch20: runs the Green Jar in Ending 3. |
| **Sergeant Bill Ostley** | Ch1: "I didn't see that." Ch5: warns Ash the lamp-wardens had a license. Ch11: takes a beating for refusing Mabry's orders. Ch13: brings the Fringe watch-house out on Lantern Night. |

**Rule:** threats to the Lane are the most personal stakes in the campaign. Use them sparingly and make each one count. **No Lane member dies by script** (loss level B covers Hester and Umbari only).

## 4. Enchanters' Row: gift opportunities

Gifts are relationship beats. When Ash commissions one, write the gift, the giver, the recipient and the inscription in the Campaign Bible's "Gifts given" list. Each gift should come back once, later, in a scene.

| When | Natural gift moment | Example | The callback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ch2–4 | Ash's first big purse (contest, bounty) | **Nell Carter:** a blanket that's always warm (Hearthglow) | Ch4: Nell is found under it in the flood, warm |
| Ch5 | After Aggie is hurt | **Aggie:** a mug that keeps tea hot (Hearthglow) | Ch20 (Ending 3): she drinks from it at the Green Jar counter |
| Ch7 | Lark's first nights in Eyrland | **Lark:** a lamp that glows her favorite color (the Lamplit, from Clara, unknowing) | Lark keeps it in Stillwater-dark places; it's how Clara first feels Lark (Ch11) |
| Ch7 | Gideon's oath and Bearback | **Gideon:** a cloak that's always dry (the Dry Cloak) | Ch10: snow on Bearback |
| Ch9 | After a Tollhaven win | **Zeke:** a pen that never blots, or a never-empty ink pot (Quickhand) | Ch17: he writes the Hall's translation with it |
| Ch11 | Ford Festival | **Clara:** a locket with a moving picture of the brothers (Keepsake & Locket) | Ch20: she holds it when she sings |
| Ch13 | Lantern Night (gift-giving custom) | **Moss:** a compass that points to one person, with Ash's hair (Keepsake & Locket) | Ch20: wherever Moss ends up, the compass points there |
| Any | Gideon's never-empty flask (Bottomless Barrel), Peg's self-stirring pot, Walt's warm boots, Pip's coin that always lands the way you want (Lightfinger) | | |

**Ending 1 and 2 note:** glimmer-cored Row gifts die when glimmer dies. **Tell the player this in the epilogue, and make it beautiful:** the gifts go dark, the people keep them anyway.

## 7. Moss's power-return milestones

Moss levels with the party as a Circle of the Moon druid. These are **story upgrades**, not extra class levels.

| # | When | Upgrade |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ch3 (veil released) | Speak with animals and plants at will. Advantage to sense Wellgates. |
| 2 | Ch6 (true form) | Once per tier, the Hart for one round as a narrative action: carry the party, break a line, face a Firstbeast. |
| 3 | Ch10 (Bearback shrine piece) | *Commune with nature* and *speak with plants* at will. Antlers visible as a shadow. |
| 4 | Ch16 (Tuskhold) | Antlers permanently visible. Fight in true form one full round per encounter (use a CR-appropriate "Hart" stat block, to be written in step 6). |
| 5 | Ch17 (Aranhollow's shrine piece) or Ch19 (Ommu's Rest) | Full strength in the finale: the Hart for the whole Phase 4 of the Stillness fight. |

**Setbacks:** if Ch6's escape fails, #2 is delayed. If Ch12's Kessel closing is done without Clara, #3 is lost until Ch16. If Ch17's Hall is forced, Moss drops back to #1 until Ch20.

## 8. Relationship-only beats (no plot required; drop in anywhere)

- Restday supper (every in-city session). Who's at the table changes as the campaign goes: Lark, Clara, Thistle, Brynja, Rook.
- Ash and Gideon on the roof: Gideon admits he's proud of him (once, Act II).
- Zeke teaching Lark to read; Lark teaching Zeke a warren song.
- Moss and Ash fishing the Bend at dawn. Moss tells one true story about Ash's mother each time.
- Clara at the Fenwick house for the first time: she touches the second cradle in the attic.
- Lark's birthday (she doesn't know when it is; the Lane picks a day and throws her a party).
- Brynja teaching Gideon dwarven oath-forms (sisterly, no romance).
- Granny Tull's letters, which arrive by otter.

## Consistency-pass rulings (CHG-12)
- **Hart rounds (§7):** the Ch6 shore transformation grants upgrade #2 and doesn't spend tier 2's once-per-tier round, so there's one Hart round in Ch7–10 and one in Ch11–13. Ch13's "holds the Hall with roots" is a free scripted beat. **Upgrade #4 (Ch16) replaces** the once-per-tier round with the full Act III ally block (`chapters/act3/ch16.md`). Tier 2 story-form block: `chapters/act1/ch06.md` §9; Act II one-round action: `chapters/act2/_index.md` §3.4.
- **Gift hooks placed in Act I:** Nell's Hearthglow blanket (Ch2–4, Ch4 flood callback); Aggie's Hearthglow mug (Ch5).
- **Willow Lane** floats lamps on the Bend for Tom and Elinor on the fire's anniversary in Leaffall (in addition to the three Midsummer lamps of SEC-16).
